 GTA 6 Devs Didn’t Feel the Internet Was ‘Necessary’
 Grand Theft Auto’s relationship with the internet has ended with GTA 6, as the latest game focuses more on apps. 
 The internet has been a staple of the Grand Theft Auto series for a long time. We first saw it in GTA 4, and it was heavily expanded in GTA 5, with players making all their purchases through websites. However, with the latest game, it seems the devs felt that having the internet wasn’t necessary. 
 GTA 6’s Jason and Lucia Don’t Need “Websites To Be Buying a Lot Of Shit”
 In an interview with Kotaku , Rockstar’s head of development, Rob Nelson, discussed why they felt the internet wasn’t necessary for GTA 6. Nelson first discussed how the team wanted to “lean into apps and create these apps.” He then explained that having the internet in GTA 6 wouldn’t be part of the narrative as it was in GTA 5, and the developers also wanted to focus on providing meaningful content to players rather than having them on the internet making purchases online. 
 More Insider Gaming:   Rockstar Explains Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Have a 40 FPS Mode 
 Nelson also explains that they want players to progress from petty thieves to big-time criminals, going through the grind, robbing small stores, and eventually pulling off big scores. He said, “They don’t really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically.”
 Rockstar’s head of development has also explained that it wasn’t a definite decision not to have the internet, but he remembered a conversation with Stu Petri, the head of 2D and UI, where he asked about websites, and Petri replied, “For what?” What do you need it for?’ and that was the end of the conversation. Nelson has stated, though, that it could be websites back in future games.
